L-DQN is a distributed limited-memory quasi-Newton method that supports asynchronous computations among the worker nodes. arxiv-2209-06209.title: Look Before You Leap: Improving Text-based Person Retrieval by Learning A Consistent Cross-modal Common Manifold
arxiv-2209-06209.creator: Zijie Wang, Aichun Zhu, Jingyi Xue, Xili Wan, Chao Liu, Tian Wang, Yifeng Li
arxiv-2209-06209.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zijie Wang, Aichun Zhu, Jingyi Xue, Xili Wan, Chao Liu, Tian Wang, Yifeng Li. The core problem of text-based person retrieval is how to bridge the heterogeneous gap between multi-modal data. Many previous approaches contrive to learning a latent common manifold mapping paradigm following a cross-modal distribution consensus prediction (CDCP) manner. When mapping features from distribution of one certain modality into the common manifold, feature distribution of the opposite modality is completely invisible.

arxiv-2303-13473.title: Very Basic Set theory
arxiv-2303-13473.creator: Doeko H. Homan
arxiv-2303-13473.description: Abstract . The naive conception of set is described as ”Any predicate has an extension”. Then Russell’s paradox is used to prove the inconsistency of naive set theory. Russell’s paradox reads ”No set can contain all and only those sets which do not contain themselves”. We call a set which contains itself an ‘individual’.

arxiv-2305-10261.title: On the Manin-Mumford Theorem for algebraic groups
arxiv-2305-10261.creator: Harry Schmidt and Immanuel van Santen
arxiv-2305-10261.description: Abstract . We describe the Zariski-closure of sets of torsion points in connected algebraic groups. This is a generalization of the Manin-Mumford conjecture for commutative algebraic groups proved by Hindry [ Hin88 ] . He proved that every subset with Zariski-dense torsion points is the finite union of torsion-translates of algebraic subgroups.

arxiv-2310-00635.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Neighbour Selection for VANET with Adaptive Trust Management
arxiv-2310-00635.creator: Orvila Sarker, Hong Shen, M. Ali Babar
arxiv-2310-00635.description: Abstract Successful information propagation from source to destination in Vehicular Adhoc Network (VANET) can be hampered by the presence of neighbouring attacker nodes causing unwanted packet dropping. Potential attackers change their behaviour over time and remain undetected due to the adhoc nature of VANET.

arxiv-2312-13862.title: Electric dipole spin resonance in single and two electron quantum dot defined in two-dimensional electron gas at the SrTiO 3 /LaAlO 3 interface.
arxiv-2312-13862.creator: B. Szafran, M. Zegrodnik, M. P. Nowak, R. Citro, P. Wójcik
arxiv-2312-13862.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by B. Szafran, M. Zegrodnik, M. P. Nowak, R. Citro, P. Wójcik. We investigate the energy spectrum of a single and two electron quantum dot (QD) embedded in two dimensional electron gas at the interface between SrTiO 3 and LaAlO 3 , in the presence of the external magnetic field. For this purpose the three band model of 3 ​ d 3d -electrons defined on the square lattice of Ti ions was utilized.

arxiv-2403-10862.title: Expansion of strongly interacting dipolar bosons in 1D optical lattices
arxiv-2403-10862.creator: Rhombik Roy, Andrea Trombettoni, Barnali Chakrabarti
arxiv-2403-10862.description: Abstract We numerically study the expansion dynamics of initially localized dipolar bosons in a homogeneous 1D optical lattice for different initial states. Comparison is made to interacting bosons with contact interaction. For shallow lattices the expansion is unimodal and ballistic, while strong lattices suppress tunneling. However for intermediate lattice depths a strong interplay between dipolar interaction and lattice depth occurs.

arxiv-2403-19106.title: Branching problem of tensoring two Verma modules and its application to differential symmetry breaking operators
arxiv-2403-19106.creator: Reiji Murakami
arxiv-2403-19106.description: Abstract Kobayashi-Pevzner discovered in [Selecta Math., 2016] that the failure of the multiplicity-one property in the fusion rule of Verma modules of 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 2 \mathfrak{sl}_{2} occurs exactly when the Rankin-Cohen bracket vanishes, and classified all the corresponding parameters.

arxiv-2406-09559.title: Decoding the Diversity: A Review of the Indic AI Research Landscape
arxiv-2406-09559.creator: Sankalp KJ, Vinija Jain, Sreyoshi Bhaduri, Tamoghna Roy, Aman Chadha ∗
arxiv-2406-09559.description: Abstract This review paper provides a comprehensive overview of large language model (LLM) research directions within Indic languages. Indic languages are those spoken in the Indian subcontinent, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Bhutan, among others. These languages have a rich cultural and linguistic heritage and are spoken by over 1.5 billion people worldwide.

arxiv-2407-17364.title: Reliability on QR Codes and Reed-Solomon Codes
arxiv-2407-17364.creator: Bhavuk Sikka Bajaj
arxiv-2407-17364.description: Abstract This study addresses the use of Reed-Solomon error correction codes in QR codes to enhance resilience against failures. To fully grasp this approach, a basic cryptographic context is provided, necessary for understanding Reed-Solomon codes. The study begins by defining a code and explores key outcomes for codes with additional properties, such as linearity.

arxiv-2411-05025.title: LLMs as Research Tools: A Large Scale Survey of Researchers’ Usage and Perceptions
arxiv-2411-05025.creator: Zhehui Liao, Maria Antoniak, Inyoung Cheong, Evie Yu-Yen Cheng, Ai-Heng Lee, Kyle Lo, Joseph Chee Chang, Amy X. Zhang
arxiv-2411-05025.description: Abstract . The rise of large language models (LLMs) has led many researchers to consider their usage for scientific work. Some have found benefits using LLMs to augment or automate aspects of their research pipeline, while others have urged caution due to risks and ethical concerns.

pmc-12853130.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cells generate purine nucleotides through de novo purine biosynthesis (DNPB) and purine salvage. Purine salvage represses DNPB to prevent excessive purine nucleotide synthesis through mechanisms that are incompletely understood. We identified Nudix hydrolase 5 (NUDT5) as a DNPB regulator. During purine salvage, NUDT5 suppresses DNPB independently of its catalytic function but through interaction with phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate amidotransferase (PPAT), the rate-limiting enzyme in the DNPB pathway.
